metadata.description: A Unique name used for the Virtual Machine domain and also for generating resource names. Defaults to a value prefixed with "aiovm-".
Type of authentication to use on the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
SSH key or password for the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
The size of the VM, at least 16GB RAM is required

variables.$fxv#0:
#cloud-config

package_upgrade: true
apt:
  preserve_sources_list: true
  sources:
    msft.list:
      source: 'deb [signed-by=$KEY_FILE] https://packages.microsoft.com/ubuntu/24.04/prod noble main'
      keyid: BC528686B50D79E339D3721CEB3E94ADBE1229CF
    azurecli.list:
      source: 'deb [signed-by=$KEY_FILE] https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/azure-cli noble main'
      keyid: BC528686B50D79E339D3721CEB3E94ADBE1229CF
    kubernetes.list:
      source: 'deb [signed-by=$KEY_FILE] https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.32/deb/ /'
      keyid: DE15B14486CD377B9E876E1A234654DA9A296436

packages:
  - azure-cli

write_files:
  - path: /etc/motd
    owner: root:root
    permissions: "0644"
    content: |
      ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
      ║               AZURE IOT OPERATIONS PROVISIONING             ║
      ╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
      ║ VM is not provisioned.                                      ║
      ║                                                             ║
      ║ To set up this VM, please do the following:                 ║
      ║   1. Run 'az login' to authenticate                         ║
      ║   2. Then run the provisioning script:                      ║
      ║      sudo /opt/provision_iot_ops.sh                         ║
      ║                                                             ║
      ║ For live status updates, run:                               ║
      ║   watch cat /etc/motd                                       ║
      ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

  - path: /opt/provision_iot_ops.sh
    owner: "1000:1000"   # Use numeric UID/GID for the non-root user
    permissions: "0755"
    content: |
      #!/bin/bash
      #
      # ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
      # ║               AZURE IOT OPERATIONS PROVISIONER              ║
      # ║    Automated setup of Kubernetes and Azure IoT Operations   ║
      # ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
      #
      # Set up the basic user environment (Assumes a non-root user with UID 1000 exists)
      MYUSER=$(id -un 1000)
      MYHOME=$(eval echo ~$MYUSER)

      # Global constant: total number of provisioning steps
      TOTAL_STEPS=12

      # Check for interactive Azure CLI login
      if ! az account show >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo -e "\033[1;31mERROR\033[0m: You are not logged in to Azure CLI. Please run 'az login' and re-run this script."
          exit 1
      fi

      #━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
      # Helper Functions: MOTD Dashboard Updates (with Step X of Y)
      #━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

      update_status() {
          local step="$1"
          local msg="$2"
          shift 2
          local details=("$@")
          {
            echo "╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
            echo "║               AZURE IOT OPERATIONS PROVISIONING             ║"
            echo "╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣"
            printf "║ Step   : %-2s of %-2s                                       ║\n" "$step" "$TOTAL_STEPS"
            printf "║ Status : %-50s ║\n" "$msg"
            if [ ${#details[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "╠────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╣"
              for detail in "${details[@]}"; do
                  printf "║ %-62s ║\n" "$detail"
              done
            fi
            echo "╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"
          } > /etc/motd
      }

      final_status() {
          local status="$1"
          local msg="$2"
          {
            # Create a marker file indicating provisioning is complete
            sudo touch /etc/azure-iot-ops-provisioned
            echo "╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗"
            echo "║               AZURE IOT OPERATIONS PROVISIONING             ║"
            echo "╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣"
            printf "║ %-62s ║\n" "$status"
            printf "║ %-62s ║\n" "$msg"
            echo "║                                                             ║"
            echo "║ VM provisioned. To manage your environment, run:            ║"
            echo "║   k9s --namespace azure-iot-operations                      ║"
            echo "╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝"
          } > /etc/motd
      }

      #━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
      # Provisioning Workflow (Background Process)
      #━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━��━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

      run_provisioning() {

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 1: Set up Repositories                              │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "1" "Setting up repositories" "Adding Microsoft and Kubernetes repositories"
          echo "Adding Microsoft repository..."
          wget -q https://packages.microsoft.com/config/ubuntu/24.04/packages-microsoft-prod.deb
          sudo dpkg -i packages-microsoft-prod.deb
          rm packages-microsoft-prod.deb
          echo "Adding Kubernetes repository..."
          sudo mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
          curl -fsSL https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.32/deb/Release.key | sudo gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes.gpg > /dev/null
          echo "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg] https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.32/deb/ /" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kubernetes.list

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 2: Install Packages                                 │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "2" "Installing packages" "Updating apt lists" "Installing Docker, kubectl, and utilities"
          while sudo fuser /var/lib/dpkg/lock >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
                sudo fuser /var/lib/apt/lists/lock >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
                sudo fuser /var/cache/apt/archives/lock >/dev/null 2>&1; do
              sleep 5
          done
          sudo apt-get update -y || { sleep 10; sudo apt-get update -y; }
          if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends docker.io || { sleep 10; sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends docker.io; }
          fi
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends kubectl git wget curl jq gnupg lsb-release

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 3: Ensure Docker is Running                         │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "3" "Starting Docker" "Enabling and starting Docker daemon"
          sudo systemctl enable docker
          sudo systemctl start docker
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
              if docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  break
              fi
              [ $i -eq 30 ] && { final_status "⚠️ FAILED" "Docker did not start properly."; exit 1; }
              sleep 1
          done

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 4: Install K3d and K9s                              │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "4" "Installing K3d and K9s" "Installing k3d and setting up cluster tools"
          if ! command -v k3d >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k3d-io/k3d/main/install.sh | bash
              if ! command -v k3d >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  final_status "⚠️ FAILED" "k3d installation failed."; exit 1;
              fi
          fi
          if ! command -v k9s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              K9S_VERSION=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/derailed/k9s/releases/latest | grep -Po '"tag_name": "v\K[^"]*')
              [ -z "$K9S_VERSION" ] && K9S_VERSION="0.27.4"
              curl -sL https://github.com/derailed/k9s/releases/download/v${K9S_VERSION}/k9s_Linux_amd64.tar.gz | tar xz -C /tmp
              sudo mv /tmp/k9s /usr/local/bin/
              sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/k9s
          fi

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 5: Install Helm                                     │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "5" "Installing Helm" "Setting up Helm package manager"
          if ! command -v helm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/master/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
              if ! command -v helm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  final_status "⚠️ FAILED" "Helm installation failed."; exit 1;
              fi
          fi

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 6: Detect Azure Resources                           │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "6" "Detecting Azure resources" "Gathering VM metadata"
          az config set extension.use_dynamic_install=yes_without_prompt
          VM_METADATA=$(curl -s -H Metadata:true --noproxy "*" "http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance?api-version=2021-02-01")
          [ -z "$VM_METADATA" ] && { final_status "⚠️ FAILED" "VM metadata retrieval failed."; exit 1; }
          SUBSCRIPTION_ID=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.subscriptionId')
          RESOURCE_GROUP=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.resourceGroupName')
          LOCATION=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.location')
          VM_NAME=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.name')
          RESOURCE_NAME="${VM_NAME}-k8s"
          update_status "6" "Azure environment detected" \
              "Subscription: $SUBSCRIPTION_ID" \
              "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
              "Location: $LOCATION" \
              "VM Name: $VM_NAME" \
              "K8s Resource: $RESOURCE_NAME"

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 7: Create K3d Cluster                               │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "7" "Creating K3d cluster" "Setting up cluster 'k3s-default'" "Ports: 1883, 8883, 8884"
          if k3d cluster list 2>/dev/null | grep -q k3s-default; then
              if k3d kubeconfig get k3s-default > /dev/null 2>&1; then
                  CLUSTER_RECREATED=false
              else
                  k3d cluster delete k3s-default
                  CLUSTER_RECREATED=true
              fi
          else
              CLUSTER_RECREATED=true
          fi
          [ "$CLUSTER_RECREATED" = true ] && { 
              k3d cluster create k3s-default \
                  -p '1883:1883@loadbalancer' \
                  -p '8883:8883@loadbalancer' \
                  -p '8884:8884@loadbalancer' \
                  --registry-create k3d-registry.localhost:127.0.0.1:5000 \
                  --wait || { final_status "⚠️ FAILED" "K3d cluster creation failed."; exit 1; }
          }

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 8: Configure kubectl                                │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "8" "Configuring kubectl" "Creating kubeconfig in \$MYHOME/.kube"
          mkdir -p "$MYHOME/.kube"
          k3d kubeconfig get k3s-default > "$MYHOME/.kube/config"
          sudo chown -R "$MYUSER":"$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/.kube"
          chmod 600 "$MYHOME/.kube/config"
          kubectl get nodes || { final_status "⚠️ FAILED" "kubectl configuration failed."; exit 1; }
          grep -q "alias k9s" "$MYHOME/.bashrc" || echo 'alias k9s="KUBECONFIG=$MYHOME/.kube/config k9s"' >> "$MYHOME/.bashrc"

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 9: Connect Kubernetes to Azure Arc                  │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "9" "Connecting to Azure Arc" "Linking Kubernetes to Azure" "Resource: $RESOURCE_NAME"
          az extension add --upgrade --name connectedk8s --yes
          ARC_CONNECTED=$(az connectedk8s show --name "$RESOURCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" 2>/dev/null)
          [ -z "$ARC_CONNECTED" ] && { 
              az connectedk8s connect --name "$RESOURCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --location "$LOCATION" || { 
                  final_status "⚠️ FAILED" "Azure Arc connection failed."; exit 1; }
          }

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 10: Create Storage Account                          │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          UNIQUE_HASH=$(echo "$VM_NAME-$SUBSCRIPTION_ID" | md5sum | head -c 8)
          STORAGE_ACCOUNT="stiot${UNIQUE_HASH}"
          STORAGE_ACCOUNT=$(echo "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
          update_status "10" "Creating storage account" "Account: $STORAGE_ACCOUNT" "Resource Group: $RESOURCE_GROUP"
          STORAGE_EXISTS=$(az storage account show --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" 2>/dev/null)
          [ -z "$STORAGE_EXISTS" ] && { 
              az storage account create --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --location "$LOCATION" --enable-hierarchical-namespace true --sku Standard_LRS || { 
                  final_status "⚠️ FAILED" "Storage account creation failed."; exit 1; }
          }

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 11: Initialize IoT Ops                              │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "11" "Initializing IoT Ops" "Deploying IoT Ops components" "Cluster: $RESOURCE_NAME"
          IOT_OPS_INITIALIZED=$(kubectl get ns azure-iot-operations 2>/dev/null)
          [ -z "$IOT_OPS_INITIALIZED" ] && { 
              az iot ops init --cluster "$RESOURCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" || { 
                  final_status "⚠️ FAILED" "IoT Ops initialization failed."; exit 1; }
          }

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Step 12: Create IoT Ops Instance                         │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          SR_ID=$(az iot ops schema registry show --name "sriot${UNIQUE_HASH}" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv 2>/dev/null)
          INSTANCE_NAME="${RESOURCE_NAME}-instance"
          update_status "12" "Creating IoT Ops instance" "Instance: $INSTANCE_NAME" "Schema Registry: sriot${UNIQUE_HASH}"
          IOT_INSTANCE_EXISTS=$(az iot ops instance show --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" 2>/dev/null)
          [ -z "$IOT_INSTANCE_EXISTS" ] && { 
              az iot ops instance create --cluster "$RESOURCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" --sr-resource-id "$SR_ID" --broker-frontend-replicas 1 --broker-frontend-workers 1 --broker-backend-part 1 --broker-backend-workers 1 --broker-backend-rf 1 --broker-mem-profile Low || { 
                  final_status "⚠️ FAILED" "IoT Ops instance creation failed."; exit 1; }
          }

          #╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
          #│ Finalization: Wait for Pods to be Ready                  │
          #╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
          update_status "12" "Finalizing" "Waiting for all pods to be ready..."
          RETRIES=0
          MAX_RETRIES=20
          while [ $RETRIES -lt $MAX_RETRIES ]; do
              NON_RUNNING=$(kubectl get pods -A | grep -v "Running\|Completed" | grep -v "^NAMESPACE" | wc -l)
              [ "$NON_RUNNING" -eq "0" ] && break
              sleep 30
              RETRIES=$((RETRIES+1))
          done

          final_status "✅ SETUP COMPLETE!" "Your Azure IoT Ops environment is ready."
      }

      # Launch the provisioning workflow in the background
      run_provisioning &

      # In the foreground, continuously display the MOTD dashboard
      watch cat /etc/motd

runcmd:
  - |
    MYUSER=$(id -un 1000)
    MYHOME=$(eval echo ~$MYUSER)
    cp /opt/provision_iot_ops.sh "$MYHOME/provision_iot_ops.sh"
    chown $MYUSER:$MYUSER "$MYHOME/provision_iot_ops.sh"
    echo "✅ Azure IoT Operations environment setup script has been installed."
